country.name: Singapore
country.kicker: A small island. An outsized influence.

overview.summary: A city, an island, and a country, built at the crossroads of Asia. With few natural resources, Singapore turned its location and connections into its greatest assets.
overview.geography: Just off the southern tip of Malaysia, across a narrow strait from Indonesia. Its position links the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea.

whyItMatters.title: A meeting point for the world
whyItMatters.text: Ships, money, and ideas pass through this small island on their way between Asia and the rest of the world.

whyItMatters.title: A different nation-building story
whyItMatters.text: Independent since 1965, it pairs a global economy with public housing, deliberate planning, and a strong state.

stories.question: How did a tiny island become so wealthy?
stories.summary: Location opened the door. Decades of deliberate choices made it valuable.

sections.title: Start with a port
sections.text: A British trading post established in 1819 connected Singapore to expanding regional trade. A deep-water harbor near a vital sea passage attracted merchants and migrants.

sections.title: Build what the world needs
sections.text: After independence, Singapore invested in housing, education, infrastructure, and export manufacturing. Foreign investment connected local workers to global production.

sections.title: Move up the value chain
sections.text: Finance, advanced manufacturing, and business services grew around that foundation. Wealth is substantial, but so are pressures around inequality, housing, and reliance on migrant labor.

stories.takeaway: Singapore did not escape geography. It built institutions and infrastructure that made its geography more valuable.

stories.question: Why is Singapore a shipping crossroads?
stories.summary: The island sits beside one of the shortest sea routes between East Asia and the Indian Ocean.

sections.title: A narrow passage, a global connection
sections.text: The Malacca and Singapore straits funnel shipping between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea. Singapore sits at the eastern end of this passage.

sections.title: More than passing ships
sections.text: A transshipment hub transfers containers between ships. Reliable terminals, ship services, and connections to many ports turn a good location into a network advantage.

stories.takeaway: A port matters because of both where it is and how well it connects to everywhere else.

stories.question: Why do so many Singaporeans have Chinese roots?
stories.summary: Modern Singapore grew through migration, but its identity is distinctly its own.

sections.title: A port draws people
sections.text: In the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, migrants from southern China came to work and trade. Malay, Indian, and other communities also shaped the settlement.

sections.title: One country, multiple inheritances
sections.text: Ethnic Chinese people form a majority of the resident population. English, Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil are official languages; Malay is the national language. Ethnicity, citizenship, and language are different parts of identity.

stories.takeaway: Singapore is a multilingual Southeast Asian nation, not simply a Chinese city abroad.
